title: Private Console: Tenant Egress Ledger & Reversible Throttle UI
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Design a compact, audit-safe UI in the Private Console that surfaces per-tenant egress spend (ledger view) and provides operators a reversible 'emergency throttle' control. The goal is to give Platform and Tenant Ops teams immediate visibility into cross-tenant egress, quick mitigation actions to protect shared capacity/SLA, and clear rollback paths with enforced audit trails.

Context: Several customers asked for more granular egress visibility and faster mitigation during inter-region bandwidth spikes. Current console only shows aggregated cluster egress and lacks an operational surface for safe throttling that is both reversible and auditable.

Outcomes desired:
- 3-panel ledger: recent egress events, per-tenant cumulative spend, anomaly flags.
- Emergency throttle that supports soft-limit (shape traffic) and hard-limit (block) modes with a cooldown and automated rollback policy.
- Explicit preview of customer impact before action (est. latency/cost/regression) and required approvals for destructive modes.
- Audit log entries with reason, operator, and linked runbook for compliance teams.

Constraints:
- Throttle actions should map cleanly to existing Private control plane APIs (throttle/egress-policy endpoints) and not require infra changes beyond API gating.
- UI must not expose tenant API keys or secrets. All operations go through RBAC-guarded actions logged in KMS/HSM-backed audit pipeline.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Figma prototype shows 3-panel ledger, action flyout, and approval modal.
2) Action flow includes preview, rollback timer, and audit-summary in the modal.
3) Design spec maps UI controls to API calls (throttle_start, throttle_preview, throttle_revert).
4) Accessibility: keyboard and screen-reader support for the ledger and modals.
5) Usability test (n=5 ops engineers) median task success >= 90% for throttling and reverting.
comments: 2026-03-02 | Marco Ruiz: Added initial wireframes and asked ops for edge cases where throttling interacts with Dedicated autoscaling. ACTION: ops to confirm expected autoscaler behavior.

2026-03-04 | Priya Singh (SRE): Throttle must not trigger autoscaler fallback loops; recommend a 'suppress-autoscale' flag at API level. Also need a clear rollback timer default (15m) and a force-revert button with approver logging.
2026-03-06 | Maya Chen: Implemented compact anomaly badge and color system, added 'estimated customer impact' heat-strips. Waiting on backend placeholders for preview API.
2026-03-09 | Legal (Emily Carter): For compliance, operator reason must be required for any hard-limit action. Add optional customer notification toggle.

2026-03-10 | Design Review: Positive on concept; suggested microcopy clarifications and stronger separation of preview vs apply. Request: add an 'explainability' link that shows sample traffic slice affected.
decisions: 1) Use two action modes: Soft-shape (rate-limit per-tenant) and Hard-block (drop outbound). 2) Require explicit reason and approver for Hard-block. 3) Default rollback timer = 15 minutes (configurable). 4) Expose 'simulate' preview using sampled telemetry rather than live enforcement.
tradeoffs:
- Adding 'suppress-autoscale' reduces unwanted scaling but could hide capacity issues from the autoscaler.
- Simulation preview adds complexity and requires sampled telemetry pipeline support; fallback is a static estimate if telemetry is unavailable.
- Immediate hard-block is fastest but highest risk -> require approver and longer audit retention.
next_steps: 1) Sync with Infra APIs: confirm throttle_preview endpoint and autoscale interaction (owner: Marco). 2) Implement Figma high-fidelity screens and microcopy updates (owner: Maya). 3) Backend spike for simulated preview (owner: Rohit). 4) Draft runbook and compliance checklist (owner: Asha). 5) Schedule ops usability session week of 2026-03-15.
